review.title: Egg Math Catches Cats
review.headline: Two lone cats, two egg-count lies, and a silent Alex wins anyway.
review.summary: There was only one Meowfia in each round, and the egg counts caught both. In round 1, Sphinx Drew claimed Pigeon. Blair's math showed Finley's nest had no room for Drew's egg, and the table convicted him. In round 2, Mouser Casey made a clever Hawk bluff using a real Turkey egg, but Drew's Owl report showed a Mouser had visited Finley, and Casey went down 5 votes to 1. Alex never said a word all game, threw his 11s with the majority, and won.

rounds.recap: Sphinx Drew claimed Pigeon and said he laid an egg in Finley. Finley's Eagle egg already accounted for his whole +1, as Blair pointed out. Casey then noted that Finley named Blair as Casey's visitor before Blair spoke, so Finley's Eagle claim was real. Ellis came over, and the vote on Drew was 5 to 1.

Drew's Owl report named a Kookaburra and a Mouser as Finley's visitors. Mouser Casey claimed Hawk and framed Ellis, using the egg she had really gained from Turkey Finley. Ellis was confused, but still worked out that only Casey's +1 fit a Mouser visit. The real Hawk, Blair, knew Casey was lying, and five players threw at her. Finley misread his own Turkey report and threw at Drew.

highlights.text: Blair broke Drew's Pigeon claim with simple math: an Eagle with one visitor plus a Pigeon egg would put Finley at 7, not 6.
Casey turned Ellis back: Finley named Blair as a visitor before Blair spoke, which a fake Eagle couldn't have known.
Casey's Hawk bluff used a real Turkey egg, and she corrected Ellis's nest math well enough that Ellis apologised.
Ellis knew his own report was confused but still worked out that only Casey's +1 fit the Mouser visit.

confusions.what: He first said Drew's claimed Pigeon egg 'matches my one egg', forgetting that his own Eagle egg already explained his +1.
His private note said he would pick Hawk, but he named Eagle for his Sphinx visit.
He said Casey's 5-card nest was her starting size. Casey had started the night at 4.
He thought a Turkey should gain eggs from its visitors and called Finley a 'fake Turkey' because Finley's nest didn't change. In fact the visitors gain the eggs, not the Turkey.
He assumed Casey's visit had confused him. Blair was the one who visited him; Casey visited Finley.

He read 'no eggs laid in or taken from your nest' as proof that nobody visited him. A Turkey's own nest never changes, and Drew's +1 actually supported Drew's visit. Finley threw at Farm Drew because of this.

design_notes: Silence paid off. Alex never spoke in either round and won with 48 by throwing high with the majority. In round 2, Blair was the real Hawk and knew Casey's Hawk claim was false, but never said so. Consider giving some reward for helping the table, or a cost for staying quiet.

A winning team banks every thrown card, even cards thrown at a teammate. Finley threw at Farm Drew and still banked 12. This weakens the reason to work out the right target. You could bank only cards thrown at the player who was eggsecuted, or only cards thrown at the other team.

The Turkey's dawn report says nothing about visitors, and Finley built his whole case on 'no change means no visitors'. Either tell the Turkey how many players visited, or make it clear that the Turkey's own count never changes.

Both rounds had only 1 Meowfia, and the claims could be checked against egg counts, so each cat fell fast. The Mouser's Wink was never used, even though Casey could have winked Drew after his Owl report. Pigeon, Falcon, House Cat and Floofer were never dealt. The 12-animal pool is mostly unused at 6 players.

Possible engine bug: Drew's Sphinx report showed only 'The Eagle is Finley', not the list of Farm roles in play that the card promises. Tit and Hawk also gave nothing useful in either round. A wrong Tit guess and a Hawk visit to a Farm player add nothing to the day.
